item.statement: The low plasticity of the sintered samples is caused by the high volume fraction of brittle Laves phases and oxides localized at grain boundaries, which promote crack initiation.
quotes: The samples' low plasticity was caused by the high volume fraction of Cr 2 Nb, (Fe, Cr)Nb Laves phases, and NbVO 4 –VO oxides, which localized at the grain boundaries
These phases were brittle at room temperature, and their localization promoted a crack initiation and propagation along the grain boundaries resulting in a decrease of the HEA plasticity
The coarse inclusions can act as a crack initiation source and cause fractures in the BCC-matrix that leads to a decrease of the HEA plasticity

item.statement: Increasing sintering temperature reduces the volume fraction of brittle Laves phases but causes oxide particles to coarsen, which can also act as crack initiation sites.
quotes: The volume fraction of the Laves phases decreased in the sample sintered at 1400 °C. However, the oxide particle size significantly increases, as shown in Figure 2
In the sample sintered at 1400 °C, the volume fraction of the Laves phases is lowered. However, the particle size of the oxides increases significantly
The coarse inclusions can serve as sources of crack initiation in the BCC-matrix

item.statement: The carburization of the surface layer due to interaction with the graphite die during SPS creates a distinct layer with different corrosion behavior compared to the bulk material.
quotes: under SPS, the HEA powder interacted with the carbon of the equipment that led to carburization of the surface layer

The carburized layers of the HEA SPS-samples obtained at 1200–1300 °C exhibited a narrow passivation region ΔE, and the potential increase up to >0.91 V resulted in a continuous increase of the current density
A clearly defined passivation plateau was almost absent, and the alloy components gradually dissolved, which results in general corrosion
